transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rebecca Moore (Lyra Head of Procurement), Sofia Alvarez (Lyra Legal), Daniel Park (Lyra CISO), Amit Shah (Lyra CTO)

Summary:
Lyra is running procurement review for Redwood's hosted + private deployment options. Primary blockers: MSA redlines around indemnity/limitation, DPA clauses for data residency and subprocessors, SLAs for latency and uptime, and approval for pricing against internal vendor comparatives. Lyra wants SOC 2, architecture diagram, and a clear onboarding checklist for VPC/private deployment. Next steps agreed (see action items).

Topics:
- MSA redlines (indemnity, liability cap, IP)
- DPA / data residency / subprocessors / retention
- SLAs and latency metrics for hosted + Dedicated
- VPC/on-prem onboarding and KMS integration
- Pricing: committed vs usage, pilot credits, PO timing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the procurement items and get to any legal redlines. also appreciate Rebecca getting the team together, I think we have about 55, 60 minutes?
[00:12] Rebecca: yeah, thanks Maya. we've got Sofia for legal, Daniel for security, Amit on the infra/arch side. main ask is to close MSA/DPA and get pricing approved for pilot.
[00:20] Maya: perfect. quick intros, then Liam will cover the technical onboarding and I can walk through the commercials and legal artifacts.
[00:28] Liam: hi all, quick note — I'll focus on the private deployment flow (VPC) and the hosted fallbacks, and how we handle key management and logging.
[00:35] Amit: great, on our side we run PCI adjacent workloads and need clear KMS controls and audit logs. also latency SLOs are important, our app is latency sensitive.
[00:44] Daniel: from security — SOC 2, encryption at rest and in transit, audit trail for inference requests, and subprocessor list. also, one of our requirements is no retention of raw customer PII beyond 30 days without explicit opt-in.
[00:58] Maya: understood. we can share SOC 2 report and our DPA. quick flag though — our hosted API by default stores minimal telemetry and is configurable for retention, and for private deployments customers can choose not to persist logs to Redwood.
[01:15] Sofia: on the MSA, our legal team flagged indemnity and the liability cap as non-starters in their current form. we usually expect a higher cap for SLAs tied to data loss.
[01:30] Maya: okay, can you pointer to the exact clause? are they wanting a carveout for security incidents or higher cap across the board?
[01:36] Sofia: mostly around security incidents and data breach. also the DPA needs explicit subprocessors list or a process to preapprove them.
[01:45] Liam: we can provide a current subprocessor list and a notification process for new subprocessors. for the KMS piece, Redwood supports customer-managed keys in dedicated/private deployments via KMS/HSM, and we can document the flow.
[02:02] Amit: does the KMS integrate with our on-prem HSMs or only cloud KMS? we have an on-prem HSM requirement for certain data classes.
[02:12] Liam: right now we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for cloud. for on-prem HSM, our Private on-prem package supports bring-your-own-key through HSM connectors but that would be part of the Private deployment agreement; we'll detail that in the runbook.
[02:30] Daniel: good — we need explicit language in the DPA describing key control and that Redwood cannot access plaintext models or customer data when CMK is used.
[02:41] Maya: noted — we have a standard paragraph for CMK and custody, we'll include that.
[02:50] Rebecca: on pricing, procurement needs the committed pricing for Dedicated and an estimate for hosted per-token costs. we also need an approval path for a 90-day pilot.
[03:02] Maya: we can propose a pilot: 3-week pilot with X committed throughput on Dedicated or hosted with priority routing. pricing workbook will show committed monthly cost, per-token, and an expected overage rate.
[03:15] Sofia: procurement will want to know whether the pilot requires a PO up front or if it's covered by a credit agreement.
[03:22] Maya: typically we do a simple PO for pilot commitment or a short term credit. I'll include both options.
[03:30] Daniel: SLA conversation — uptime is fine but we also need latency SLOs. what are your typical p99s for popular models for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:42] Liam: for hosted small seq text gen our p99 is around 220-450ms depending on model and context length; for Dedicated with pinned GPU pools we can get predictable sub-200ms p99 for many common seq lengths. keep in mind model choice, quantization, and batching impact those numbers.
[04:00] Amit: can we get a performance profile per model? our legal ops want to tie a latency SLA to a specific model/instance class.
[04:08] Liam: yes — we have a model catalog with performance profiles and we'll share the Redwood-verified benchmark spreadsheet. note though SLAs for latency are typically tied to a model family and config (e.g., quantized, sequence length 512).
[04:25] Sofia: on data residency — Lyra operates across EU and US. we need to confirm region guarantees and subprocessors for EU data.
[04:36] Maya: we support region pinning for Hosted — you can pin EU-only, and for Private deployments data remains in your VPC/region. our DPA includes standard EU SCCs and also we can add region-specific addenda if needed.
[04:52] Rebecca: procurement will also want a list of support SLAs, response times for Sev1/Sev2 and escalation path (phone/Slack/pager).
[05:02] Maya: our support tiers include 24x7 emergency for enterprise with phone and Slack, and typical response times are 1 hour for Sev1. we'll share the SLA doc.
[05:12] Daniel: second question on logging: we need structured audit logs for all inference calls, with redaction options, and a way to route logs to our S3 or ELK stack.
[05:23] Liam: yes — we support log forwarding, S3 sinks, and filtered/hashed logging modes. note that for hosted there are retention defaults but we can configure minimal retention. for Private, logs stay on your infra unless you opt-in to send them to Redwood.
[05:38] Maya: quick note — sometimes our transcription says 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' in docs, just a heads up on naming in the runbook.
[05:45] (brief laughter)
[06:02] Sofia: back to the MSA: limitation of liability — is Redwood able to accept a mutual cap tied to fees in the rolling 12 months? we usually push for mutual limitations.
[06:15] Maya: standard practice at Redwood is a cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months, we can make it mutual; for security incidents that cause data exposure there might be carve-outs we can discuss with legal.
[06:28] Sofia: we'd like the carve-out narrowed and to have an insurance representation clause (cyber insurance).
[06:35] Maya: we can represent cyber insurance and include certificate on request.
[06:42] Rebecca: timeline — procurement wants to finish review week of Nov 15 if possible so we can start the pilot before end of month. is that plausible?
[06:52] Maya: yes if legal returns redlines promptly and we get SOC2 and pricing over the next week, we can aim for pilot kickoff 11/16 to 11/20.
[07:03] Daniel: a few technical clarifications — do you provide per-request request IDs and tracing for correlation with our APM?
[07:10] Liam: yes, request IDs and trace headers are included and we have tracing hooks for distributed tracing. we'll include sample spans.
[07:22] Amit: what about rate limiting and throttling behavior — we need enforced quotas and burst handling documented.
[07:29] Liam: we expose per-API route quotas, burst capacity settings, and a policy for queuing vs rejecting. Dedicated customers can configure higher burst buffers.
[07:40] Sophia: speaker misattribution here, but she says — sorry Sofia: question on subprocessors notification window?
[07:48] Maya: we notify customers 30 days before new subprocessors go into production, and for sensitive ones we can provide a shorter approval window.
[07:57] Sofia: we need that in the DPA. also, add right to audit clause?
[08:04] Maya: we include SOC 2 and audit rights through an agreed process; on-prem Private deployments can include broader audit access.
[08:12] (fast forward through details where Liam walks through onboarding doc)
[09:00] Liam: so onboarding steps: 1) sign MSA/DPA 2) exchange technical questionnaire 3) provision VPC peering and KMS binding 4) pilot traffic + benchmark 5) production cutover. I'll send a one-pager checklist.
[09:15] Rebecca: procurement needs the pricing workbook to show committed vs usage, and an example invoice/PO.
[09:24] Maya: ok will include invoice template and sample SOW language for pilot.
[09:30] Sofia: are there export controls or geo restrictions on model weights? we have team in APAC.
[09:38] Liam: some open models have export/control restrictions, our catalog will flag them. for Private deployments you can bring your own model weights subject to license.
[09:48] Daniel: curious on retention defaults again — can you prevent Redwood from using data for model training?
[09:55] Maya: yes, we have a no-training pledge option and it's part of the DPA for enterprise — we can guarantee no training or model telemetry retention for customer data.
[10:05] Amit: on SLA metrics, would you accept a breach credit schedule with multiplication of monthly fees for downtime?
[10:12] Maya: yes, our SLA credits are standard: credit tiers based on downtime and we can attach those to the Dedicated contract.
[10:20] Rebecca: procurement also asked about termination assistance and export of logs and model artifacts — what's the standard?
[10:27] Liam: we provide a 90-day export window with tooling to export logs and metadata and guidance for KV cache invalidation.
[10:35] Maya: also we'll include playbooks for termination assistance.
[10:42] Sofia: one legal item — the MSA has an indemnity that references third party IP claims for generated content. we need clarity on who owns outputs and liability if an output infringes.
[10:54] Maya: good question — our standard is customer retains ownership of their inputs and outputs, but we disallow indemnities for misuse. we can add a specific clause around generated content and a mutual cooperation process for claims.
[11:08] Sofia: ok we'll review and propose language.
[11:15] (discussion moves to timeline and internal approvals)
[11:25] Rebecca: next steps for procurement — I'll run pricing to finance and need the final workbook by Friday.
[11:33] Maya: I'll send the workbook and SOC2 today and the redlined MSA by Thursday EOD.
[11:40] Daniel: security will review the DPA and get back by Monday next week.
[11:45] Amit: infra will schedule the pilot kickoff once the PO is approved.
[11:52] Maya: great — let's do a quick recap of action items.
[11:56] (recap and confirmations)
[12:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and attachments.

Notes about transcript quality: several speaker attribution hiccups and occasional ASR mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'K V cash'), name spellings occasionally off.

Attachments referenced: Redwood SOC2 report (link sent after call), MSA redline draft (to be sent), DPA template, Pricing workbook, VPC onboarding checklist, Redwood model performance spreadsheet (benchmarks).

End of transcript.
